# LIBNOVA provider and portable receiving contract

## Scope and evidence

This contract describes the independently implemented LIBNOVA destination in the existing research preservation application. The provider source was retrieved on 12 October 2026 from LIBNOVA's maintained repositories. The implementation uses the deployed container, metadata schema, storage, native File index and existing BagIt Function. It does not create an account, container, schema, Function or substitute a declared checksum for actual content receiving.

Two source revisions govern the integration:

| Source | Exact revision | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LIBNOVA SDK, repository project 79 | 2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695 | Current API objects, File iteration, metadata ADD, S3 path/index behavior and Function call. |
| BagIt validator, repository project 131 | f61b3e09d670f4a8fd49c415e5b628a335294870 | Actual unpacked-folder validation workflow and its job report. |

The captured source is a protocol reference. The application does not copy the complete upstream SDK under an assumed common license. In particular, an MIT notice on an individual file is not evidence that every upstream module has that license.

Primary source references:

- [SDK API driver](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/79/repository/files/libnova%2Fcommon%2Fapi%2FDriver.py/raw?ref=2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695).
- [Native File API and iteration](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/79/repository/files/libnova%2Fcommon%2Fapi%2FFile.py/raw?ref=2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695).
- [Existing Function invocation](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/79/repository/files/libnova%2Fcommon%2Fapi%2FFunction.py/raw?ref=2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695).
- [Original Function request structure](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/79/repository/files/libnova%2Fcommon%2Fnuclio%2FRequest.py/raw?ref=2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695).
- [S3 File implementation](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/79/repository/files/libnova%2Fcommon%2Ffilesystem%2FS3%2FFile.py/raw?ref=2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695).
- [S3 storage implementation](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/79/repository/files/libnova%2Fcommon%2Ffilesystem%2FS3%2FStorage.py/raw?ref=2e03d8ba3d10afe19f1bed450c68e77a188ad695).
- [Maintained BagIt Function](https://repo.libnova.com/api/v4/projects/131/repository/files/main.py/raw?ref=f61b3e09d670f4a8fd49c415e5b628a335294870).
- [LABDRIVE Function operation and job output](https://docs.libnova.com/labdrive/get-started/execute-lambda-functions).
- [LIBSAFE Advanced Function operation](https://docs.libnova.com/libsafe-advanced-manual/get-started/functions).
- [AWS-maintained Boto3 documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/boto3/latest/).

These are captured-source identities. A customer's present destination is separately checked at receiving time and recorded in its original operation.

## Application modules and supported inputs

The original `preservation.py` owns the source collection, review revisions and BagIt transfer. The new `libnova.py` owns the destination mapping, frozen package and standalone portable snapshot. The new `libnova_client.py` owns the receiving plan, original remote actions, observations and recovery.

A prepared package retains:

| Member | Role |
| --- | --- |
| package.json | Immutable package identity, original transfer binding, summary and exact inventory. |
| bag/ | Every unchanged original BagIt member. |
| original-bag.zip | Exact supplied original archive, when preparation received a ZIP. |
| mapping.json | Normalized selected descriptor mapping. |
| record-metadata.json | Source-bound included record IDs, mapped values and unmapped/source rights context. |
| report.html | Deterministic human review of this frozen package. |
| operations/ | Original client plans, requests, results, provider observations, reports and progress. |

The package schema is `stellar-forge.libnova-research-package.v1`. Its ID is derived from the canonical binding containing original bag identity, original manifest SHA256, every bag member's path/length/SHA256 and normalized mapping. The package's own canonical SHA256 additionally identifies the complete prepared descriptor used by each operation.

Limits for this initial profile are 1,000 included bibliographic metadata records and 1 GiB of original bag material. A portable snapshot has an 8 GiB total receiving limit, 30,000 members and bounded JSON members. These are format/input limits, not a promise of constant memory usage: the original preservation foundation reads some source and archive evidence into memory. Resource sizing must use the agreed supplied sample.

Mapping schema: `stellar-forge.libnova-research-mapping.v1`.

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.libnova-research-mapping.v1",
  "fields": [
    {"dcField": "title", "iecode": "dc.title", "dataType": "LONGSTRING"}
  ],
  "note": "Confirmed existing descriptor mapping."
}
~~~

Supported explicit descriptor types are STRING, LONGSTRING, NUMBER, DATE and BOOL, corresponding to the source enum values 1 through 5. Complex linked fields, enumerations and provider-specific relationships require a separately agreed mapping profile. The original source and Dublin Core values remain available regardless of which fields are mapped.

## Receiving configuration

Configuration schema: `stellar-forge.libnova-client.v1`.

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.libnova-client.v1",
  "baseUrl": "https://existing-platform.example",
  "tokenEnv": "LIBNOVA_API_TOKEN",
  "containerId": 101,
  "storageId": 201,
  "metadataSchemaId": 301,
  "functionId": 401,
  "objectPrefix": "reviewed-research",
  "s3": {
    "endpointUrl": "https://existing-object-endpoint.example",
    "bucket": "existing-bucket",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "accessKeyEnv": "LIBNOVA_S3_ACCESS_KEY",
    "secretKeyEnv": "LIBNOVA_S3_SECRET_KEY",
    "addressingStyle": "path"
  },
  "timeoutSeconds": 60,
  "indexWaitSeconds": 60,
  "jobWaitSeconds": 60,
  "pollSeconds": 1,
  "note": "Illustrative IDs; replace with the receiving owner's existing IDs."
}
~~~

The IDs above are examples, not a deployed destination. Optional fields are functionKey, caFile, allowLoopback and s3.sessionTokenEnv/s3.caFile. All literal credentials are excluded from configuration. The endpoint must be an origin without embedded credentials, query, fragment or API path. A custom CA file preserves verification.

The platform receives Bearer authorization. Boto3 and botocore perform the original S3 signing. The application does not implement another signer or invoke the upstream convenience storage wrapper that prints credential values. Boto3 is an explicit lazy dependency, currently constrained by the application to `boto3>=1.36,<2`. Before receiving, its service model must expose conditional PutObject.

Preflight reads the existing container, storage, schema, Function and every selected descriptor. It compares the actual provider relationships to the frozen configuration and retains a compact provider-binding.json. Subsequent receiving rejects a changed binding. For MINIO/CEPH, the configured endpoint must match the original storage's endpoint and secure flag. For AWS-style storage, the region and approved endpoint are checked along with the bucket.

HTTP is permitted only with allowLoopback:true and an explicitly entered localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 origin. The original native fixture uses ports 18083 and 18084 by convention; the application does not hardcode those ports.

## Exact native API surfaces

All paths below are relative to the saved HTTPS origin followed by `/api/`. The original API driver uses JSON conditions for GET collections. The client retains status, selected response headers, original byte length and SHA256, and sanitized JSON for every response.

| Method and path | Use and accepted evidence |
| --- | --- |
| GET container/{id} | id, storage_id and metadata_schema_id must match the saved configuration. |
| GET storage/{id} | id, S3 type and parsed extra bind provider/bucket/region/endpoint. |
| GET objects/metadata/schema/{id} | The existing schema object, allowing its native one-element wrapper. |
| GET objects/metadata/schema/descriptor | Conditions select metadata_schema_id and iecode; id/type/code/schema must match. |
| GET functions/{id} | Existing Function id/key and folder-capable source type. |
| GET file | Exact fullpath lookup or the maintained keyset folder traversal. |
| GET file/{id} | Original native identity, container, path, type and file byte size. |
| GET file/{id}/metadata | Complete repeated descriptor values. |
| PUT file/{id}/metadata | Only the explicit additive ADD body below. |
| POST container/{cid}/file/{fid}/event/{functionId} | Invoke the existing Function on the original native bag folder. |
| GET job/{id} | Original job identity, Function/container/folder binding and status/result. |
| GET job/{id}/messages | Original job messages with continuation completeness checks. |
| GET job/{id}/assets | Original report references with continuation completeness checks. |

A typical native File object contains id, container_id, parent, fullpath, type, size and deleted. File type 1 is a file, 2 a folder and 3 a journal; this receiving profile accepts only the original files and folders. Paths start with a slash; folders end with one.

Exact path lookup uses:

~~~json
{
  "conditions": [
    {"container_id": 101},
    {"fullpath": "/reviewed-research/package/operation/data/example.json"},
    {"deleted": 0}
  ],
  "limit": 2
}
~~~

Recursive folder traversal preserves the maintained File.iterate_files keyset form:

~~~json
{
  "conditions": [
    {"container_id": 101},
    {"parent": 501},
    {"deleted": 0},
    {"id": {"operator": "gt", "value": 0}}
  ],
  "limit": 1000
}
~~~

The client advances from the maximum returned native ID, rejects nonprogress, repeated IDs, foreign parents or containers, and continues until an actual empty response. An observed short page does not imply that the entire folder was read. The final recursive native ID/path closure must match the complete received bag and directories.

API success envelopes may use result or data, including the captured nested data wrapper. Explicit success:false, malformed JSON, unsupported response shapes and retained pagination indicators remain failures or receiving pauses. An unfinished collection is never reported as a complete metadata or job-output read.

## S3 bytes and File indexing

The upstream storage convention places container objects under `{containerId}/{relativePath}` in the selected bucket. This client derives an operation namespace from the configured prefix, immutable package ID and a stable hash of the original operation ID.

Before the first write, the original operation verifies that its namespace is empty both in S3 and the native File index, then durably records that admission. A new plan cannot adopt an occupied namespace. Reopening the original saved plan continues its retained admission.

Each actual bag member is uploaded from its original held file descriptor. The client checks that descriptor's bytes and SHA256 before dispatch, passes ContentLength and ContentMD5 through the maintained S3 transport, and uses IfNoneMatch:* to prevent overwriting a pre-existing object. Required folder markers are empty objects under the same namespace. No throwaway upload is used as acceptance evidence.

An immutable local action request precedes each PUT. The client disables automatic S3 write retries. If an outcome is lost, it retains the original request and reads the actual object. Matching length and SHA256 can complete the original action. An absent or different object after an uncertain original dispatch is not a reason to repeat that write automatically.

After content receiving, the client waits for the platform's own File index and freezes the returned File IDs, parent relationships, paths and original byte identities. It compares both the full S3 prefix and recursive native File tree. A database File record without its real S3 bytes cannot pass. An S3 object without its expected native File identity cannot pass.

The final read repeats actual content hashing and native identity checks. It does not treat an ETag, a hash declaration API or an upload response as content verification.

## Metadata preservation

The actual supported additive form is:

~~~json
{
  "metadata": [
    {"iecode": "dc.title", "value": "Reviewed title", "action": "ADD"},
    {"iecode": "dc.creator", "value": "First creator", "action": "ADD"},
    {"iecode": "dc.creator", "value": "Second creator", "action": "ADD"}
  ]
}
~~~

The original metadata is retained before any ADD. Mapped values are compared as multisets, preserving repeated values; original unmapped values must remain present with at least their original multiplicities. New unrelated metadata is allowed.

An already matching mapped set requires no write. A conflicting mapped set stops receiving. If a process loses an ADD response, current metadata can establish the original result. If the complete expected values are not observed, the client retains the uncertain original action and does not send another ADD. It never substitutes the upstream replacement-style metadata setter.

## Existing Function and original job

The current SDK's Function call uses:

~~~json
{
  "extra": {
    "research_package_id": "the-original-package-id",
    "research_operation_id": "the-original-operation-id"
  }
}
~~~

This body is POSTed to the container/File event endpoint for the selected Function ID. The original response carries container_id, file_id, job_id, file_path and event_key. These identities are bound to the immutable started Function action.

The client does not use Job.create as an execution shortcut. That method creates a job record and does not establish that the selected original folder was passed through the required Function call.

Original job status values are 1 RUNNING, 2 COMPLETED, 3 WAITING and 4 FAILED. Result values are 1 OK, 2 OK_WITH_WARNING and 3 ERROR. A completed warning remains visible in the final result. Unknown states are retained, not guessed to be successful.

The job must match the saved job ID, container and Function. An explicitly entered job ID additionally requires server-side file_id or a matching single-file Function input binding. A response that points at another folder or input set is rejected.

Job assets are resolved back to original native File objects, checked for container and path, and downloaded from the actual S3 key. Each observed report version is retained separately with size and SHA256. The local report path never substitutes for the original job/asset IDs.

The maintained BagIt Function operates on unpacked folders. Source review also found that its own checks are not a sufficient complete-record proof: particular missing-member paths can continue, and its extra-file traversal does not itself establish this application's full recursive closure. Therefore the application independently validates the original BagIt before upload and repeats full source/content/index/metadata receiving after the original job completes. These are implementation conclusions from the pinned Function source, not a claim about every LIBNOVA deployment.

## Durable operation and reconciliation schema

Operation schema: `stellar-forge.libnova-operation.v1`. The immutable operation.json binds id, packageId, packageSha256, normalized configuration, configurationSha256, objectPrefix and the two primary source revisions.

The on-disk operation retains provider-binding.json, namespace-admission.json, indexed-files.json, metadata-baselines, immutable observations, original action request/result pairs, downloaded job assets, receiving proofs/reports and atomic state.json.

| API | Side effects |
| --- | --- |
| plan(workspace, configuration, operation_id) | Offline local immutable plan and initial state. |
| load_operation(workspace, operation_id) | Pure package/configuration binding read. |
| show(workspace, operation_id) | Pure atomic saved-state read; no writer lock or provider request. |
| run(workspace, operation_id) | Original planned provider writes plus receiving observations. |
| refresh(workspace, operation_id) | Provider reads and local observations; no new PUT/ADD/Function. |
| reconciliation_template(kind) | Pure provider-owned evidence template. |
| reconcile(workspace, operation_id, evidence) | Read-only provider validation plus original local result recording. |

Every operation writer and package export holds `libnova.lock(prepared)`. It is nonblocking: a concurrent writer gets WORKSPACE_BUSY. The observer can read the current atomic state while the original remote request is in progress.

Every action result must match the SHA256 of its immutable original request and the operation/package identity. The action directory name is derived from the action key. Unknown outcomes remain recorded; there is no automatic switch to another operation ID.

Evidence schema: `stellar-forge.libnova-operation.v1.reconciliation`.

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.libnova-operation.v1.reconciliation",
  "kind": "original-function-response",
  "response": {
    "container_id": 101,
    "file_id": 501,
    "job_id": 601,
    "file_path": "/original/bag/folder/",
    "event_key": "original-returned-key"
  },
  "note": "Location and origin of the original returned response."
}
~~~

The other supported form replaces response with `kind:original-job-id` and a positive integer jobId. Both require a nonempty source note. The client supplies both templates; the Workbench consumes them rather than defining a competing evidence schema.

Saved state schema is `stellar-forge.libnova-operation.v1.state`, with operationId, state, updatedAt and phase-specific data. show returns {operation,state,networkRequests:0,mutation:false,stateRead}; run, refresh and reconcile return the state record directly. A later failed observation preserves its prior verified observation as historical evidence rather than implying that the old result is current.

VERIFIED includes the complete receiving proof path/length/SHA256, report path, source/included/excluded counts, object/byte counts, native container/schema/job IDs and explicit allOriginalBytesVerified/allMappedMetadataVerified flags. The proof contains every included original identifier, source SHA256, native File ID, content length/SHA256 and mapped values.

## Portable receiving and interruption behavior

Standalone export includes all frozen package files and original operation history, plus the mandatory application closure: preservation.py, libnova.py, libnova_client.py, libnova-requirements.txt and research/oai/oai_feed.py. Operator/provider guides are included when present. The full Workbench export additionally includes its original source/review/operator context and managed entry.

The snapshot manifest lists the exact path, byte length and SHA256 of every member. Receiving refuses duplicate, encrypted, special, unsafe or unlisted ZIP members, validates all hashes and CRCs, and requires the mandatory application files.

The receiver holds the original regular archive descriptor for hashing, ZIP access and the final publication checks. It uses a deterministic output-bound staging directory and an immutable archive/manifest binding. Its own interrupted metadata temporary can be adopted only when the stage is empty or contains the expected incomplete binding prefix. Unrelated retained bytes are never removed or adopted.

Per-member extraction publishes only completed, fsynced bytes. A repeated original receive reuses verified completed files and its own bound staging state, then atomically publishes the whole directory. The binding remains present through that final rename so process loss at the boundary stays recoverable.

Reopening an already received directory verifies its original archive binding, immutable source/application and every original operation member. Atomic state may advance; new legitimate observations and operations may be added. All original/current operation identities are validated through the pure client read. A removed original operation.json or altered original request cannot be hidden by an otherwise valid bag.

## Native acceptance record

One owned original169 receiving journey should exercise the actual HTTP and boto3/S3 transport, delayed native indexing, descriptor validation and additive metadata, original Function response/job/report, all-record byte proof, interrupted original action reconciliation and complete export/cold receive. It should retain the exact fixture source, provider IDs, command, logs, source versions, response counts, no-duplicate-write assertions and final artifact hashes.

That fixture is an application/protocol observation. Live tenant acceptance requires the receiving institution's existing destination, explicit credentials and source/mapping agreement. Final handoff must state which of these actually completed and link its exact retained receipt.

# Python 3.11+; only the LIBNOVA S3 receiving path imports this dependency.
# boto3 supplies its compatible botocore signer and S3 service model.
boto3>=1.36,<2

# LIBNOVA reviewed research receiving

## What this workflow delivers

This application takes a saved, reviewed bibliographic collection from the existing research preservation workspace and prepares it for one existing LIBSAFE Advanced or LABDRIVE container. It preserves the original source pages, record identifiers, review decisions, rights notes and all original BagIt members. The receiving operation uploads the unpacked bag, waits for the platform's own File index, applies the explicitly selected descriptor values, invokes an existing BagIt Function once and records its original job and reports.

A completed receiving state includes actual downloaded content lengths and SHA256 values for every original object, the platform File IDs and paths, the complete indexed folder, and a comparison of each mapped metadata value. Job completion and content verification are separate observations. A job that reports success cannot by itself establish that all source records arrived.

The initial supported workshare is one source profile, one existing container, one existing metadata schema, its associated storage and one existing BagIt Function. Its supplied-sample acceptance envelope is up to 1,000 bibliographic metadata records and 1 GiB of source/export material. This is a reviewed metadata collection; article texts, images and media described by the records retain their own rights and are not implicitly included or licensed.

The maintained application source is complete. The original 169-record public-source receiving journey and tenant acceptance must be identified by their actual receipts. Do not describe a prepared command, a successful source review or a local fixture as acceptance by a customer's live tenant.

## Start with the existing workspace

Use the installed research preservation application and its original source example. The complete source example is the 169-record OpenAlex metadata archive identified by SHA256 948c5c85a3ec88cf26ab9bae2ebcda284ea429dfa3c8240ac2565e30b278f77b. Its declared source closure retains the original source pages and full original manifest as provenance. It does not substitute another customer's export or the later paid research collection.

The original preservation engine provides the review history and BagIt producer. LIBNOVA adds a destination package and a receiving operation. It does not replace the source collection, infer new rights, create a tenant, create a container or install a remote Function.

Use Python 3.11 or later. The producer and offline source review use the standard library. Actual S3 receiving additionally uses the declared boto3 dependency and its compatible botocore implementation. Install from the supplied requirements file in your existing application environment:

~~~sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/preservation/libnova-requirements.txt
~~~

The S3 dependency is imported only when that destination's client runs. Existing RODA and Preservica workflows remain available without importing it. The client checks that the installed S3 model supports conditional PutObject before it dispatches any upload. The native receiving report should record the actual Python, boto3 and botocore versions used; the requirements range is not a claim that a particular installation has already passed.

## Review and freeze the source

In the browser Workbench, open the existing reviewed collection, inspect the saved inclusion decisions and select its published review before preparing LIBNOVA. The original source remains visible. A correction produces another saved review, and its transfer has its own revision-bound identity.

The equivalent original commands are:

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/preservation.py init \
  --source /absolute/OpenAlex_CIIM_Source_Example_20261012.zip \
  --workspace /absolute/research-review \
  --organization "Receiving institution" \
  --contact "Receiving team"

python3 research/preservation/preservation.py review-template \
  --workspace /absolute/research-review > /absolute/review.json

python3 research/preservation/preservation.py review-save \
  --workspace /absolute/research-review \
  --input /absolute/review.json --expected-revision 0

python3 research/preservation/preservation.py build \
  --workspace /absolute/research-review \
  --output /absolute/reviewed-transfer.zip \
  --expected-revision 1 --zip
~~~

The revision numbers above illustrate a fresh workspace. Use the actual current revision returned by the original application. Do not force an old revision over a later saved review. If the collection is already initialized and reviewed, continue that workspace and omit the initialization step.

The transfer preserves one JSON content file for each included work, the reviewed Dublin Core values and the original source/review evidence. Excluded records remain explained in the source and decision history. Contact and organization fields are part of the frozen transfer identity, rather than mutable decorations on an already published bag.

## Map existing metadata descriptors

Generate the destination mapping:

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova.py mapping-template > /absolute/libnova-mapping.json
~~~

Its schema is `stellar-forge.libnova-research-mapping.v1`:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.libnova-research-mapping.v1",
  "fields": [
    {"dcField": "title", "iecode": "dc.title", "dataType": "LONGSTRING"},
    {"dcField": "creator", "iecode": "dc.creator", "dataType": "LONGSTRING"}
  ],
  "note": "Codes and types confirmed against the receiving container's existing schema."
}
~~~

The example descriptor codes are placeholders. Enter the codes already deployed in the selected metadata schema. The receiving client checks each code, schema ID and data type against the current provider response before making the first upload.

| Mapping field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| dcField | The reviewed Dublin Core field from the original record. |
| iecode | An existing LIBNOVA descriptor code. |
| dataType | STRING, LONGSTRING, NUMBER, DATE or BOOL, matching the existing descriptor. |
| note | The agreed mapping basis and any intentionally unmapped fields. |

A Dublin Core field can have repeated values. The mapping preserves those values and their multiplicity. NUMBER, DATE and BOOL inputs must be accepted by the explicit type conversion rules; ambiguous conversion is an input error. Unmapped Dublin Core fields remain in the original source and bag metadata. They are not silently discarded.

Remote metadata writes use additive ADD operations. The client captures the original metadata before the first ADD, compares the complete mapped value multiset and checks that original unmapped values remain present. If mapped descriptors already contain different values, it stops for reconciliation instead of replacing them.

Prepare and verify the complete destination package:

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova.py prepare \
  --bag /absolute/reviewed-transfer.zip \
  --mapping /absolute/libnova-mapping.json \
  --out /absolute/libnova-package

python3 research/preservation/libnova.py verify \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package

python3 research/preservation/libnova.py show \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package
~~~

Preparation freezes the mapping, retains the complete original ZIP when supplied, reproduces every original bag member, derives the mapped record metadata and writes a human review. The package identifier binds the original review/transfer identity, exact bag inventory and normalized mapping. Changing any of those inputs requires a different prepared package.

## Configure an existing receiving destination

Generate the client configuration:

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py configuration-template \
  > /absolute/libnova-configuration.json
~~~

| Required input | Receiving meaning |
| --- | --- |
| baseUrl | The existing platform HTTPS origin, without an API path or embedded credentials. |
| containerId | The selected existing container. |
| storageId | That container's existing S3 storage. |
| metadataSchemaId | That container's existing metadata schema. |
| functionId | The existing Function that accepts the bag folder. |
| objectPrefix | The agreed relative parent path; the client adds package and operation identity beneath it. |
| tokenEnv | Name of the environment variable holding the authorized API token. |
| s3.endpointUrl, bucket, region | The actual endpoint and bucket for the selected storage. |
| s3.accessKeyEnv, secretKeyEnv | Environment variable names for authorized S3 credentials. |
| s3.sessionTokenEnv | Optional environment variable name for a temporary S3 session token. |
| s3.addressingStyle | The existing endpoint's path or virtual addressing mode. |

Credentials are environment references. Do not place token or secret values in the JSON, source repository, review notes or screenshots. The client uses the platform's original Bearer token and boto3's standard SigV4 implementation. TLS verification remains enabled; an optional CA file can be supplied for an existing private certificate authority.

The initial example contains no real tenant IDs or credentials. Obtain the existing destination IDs, storage agreement, descriptor mapping and authorized access from the receiving owner. The client validates the container-to-storage and container-to-schema relationships, the Function identity and its folder-capable source type, the storage endpoint and bucket, and every mapped descriptor.

`allowLoopback:true` permits HTTP only for explicitly entered localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1 receiving fixtures. It does not relax production HTTPS. The supplied native receiving runner uses this option with its own local fixture and harmless fixture credentials.

## Plan once, then run the original operation

Choose an operation ID that remains stable throughout this receiving attempt and its recovery:

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py plan \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package \
  --configuration /absolute/libnova-configuration.json \
  --operation-id research-collection-original-001

python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py run \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package \
  --operation-id research-collection-original-001
~~~

Planning is offline. It freezes the package, configuration and operation namespace and creates no remote object or job. Repeating the same plan reopens that saved identity. A different configuration under the same operation ID is rejected.

Actual receiving follows these stages:

1. Validate the current existing destination and mapped descriptors.
2. Admit the empty operation namespace and retain that original admission.
3. Upload the actual unpacked bag and required directory markers with conditional object creation.
4. Read back every uploaded object's size and SHA256, then wait for the platform's native File index.
5. Freeze the original File IDs, paths and parent relationships and compare the complete S3 and native folder inventories.
6. Apply the selected descriptor values with the retained additive metadata actions.
7. Invoke the chosen existing BagIt Function on the original bag folder once, retain its response and follow that job.
8. Receive the original job messages and report assets, then independently recheck all source bytes and mapped values before recording VERIFIED.

The maintained Function endpoint is the container/File event endpoint, not a standalone job-record creation endpoint. The Function receives the unpacked native folder; uploading a ZIP alone does not produce the equivalent receiving input.

Every writer holds the prepared workspace's original lock. If another original operation still holds it, a second writer reports WORKSPACE_BUSY. The browser can continue to show the last saved atomic progress: `show` makes no provider request and does not wait for the remote writer.

## Read progress and recover without duplicate writes

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py show \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package \
  --operation-id research-collection-original-001

python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py refresh \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package \
  --operation-id research-collection-original-001
~~~

`show` is an offline saved-state read. `refresh` makes provider reads and records new observations but does not dispatch another PUT, metadata ADD or Function invocation. A waiting or reconciliation result is a meaningful retained state, not a reason to invent another operation ID.

| State or condition | Operator action |
| --- | --- |
| PLANNED | Review the saved inputs, then run the original operation. |
| WAITING_INDEX | Keep the existing objects and use refresh after indexing progresses. |
| WAITING_JOB or WAITING_JOB_ASSETS | Follow the original saved job and receive its output. |
| REQUIRES_RUN | No original write exists yet; use run after reviewing the saved plan. |
| RECONCILE_REQUIRED | Inspect retained request/response evidence and reconcile that original action. |
| REMOTE_*_MISMATCH | Preserve the observation and correct the receiving conflict with its owner. |
| ORIGINAL_JOB_FAILED | Inspect the original job and reports. A new job is a deliberate subsequent operation. |
| VERIFIED | Export the complete workspace and retain its full receiving proof. |

Each provider write has an immutable request record published before dispatch. If a process stops after dispatch but before the response is retained, the next invocation reopens that request. It does not repeat an uncertain object write or metadata ADD. Exact content or metadata readback can complete the original recorded action. If an uncertain Function lacks a retained response, the operator must provide the original response or an existing job ID whose server-side binding establishes the selected folder.

Generate the appropriate evidence form from the provider client:

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py reconciliation-template \
  --kind original-function-response > /absolute/reconcile.json

python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py reconciliation-template \
  --kind original-job-id > /absolute/reconcile-job.json
~~~

The first form contains `response` with the original container_id, file_id, job_id, file_path and event_key. The second contains a positive integer `jobId`. Both require a note identifying the original evidence. Do not copy a different job ID or fabricate a successful response.

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova_client.py reconcile \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package \
  --operation-id research-collection-original-001 \
  --evidence /absolute/reconcile.json
~~~

Reconciliation verifies the original Function request, container, Function and folder. It saves the accepted evidence and original result. Follow with refresh to receive the original job's current outputs and complete the full byte and metadata proof.

Provider transport errors, limits and unsupported pagination remain visible. A response with an unconsumed continuation cannot establish a complete job-message, asset or metadata collection. The client retains sanitized provider observations and original raw-response hashes. Credential-bearing fields and configured secret values are excluded from saved text.

## Export, receive and reopen the complete application

~~~sh
python3 research/preservation/libnova.py export \
  --workspace /absolute/libnova-package \
  --out /absolute/LIBNOVA_Research_Receiving_001.zip

python3 research/preservation/libnova.py receive \
  --source /absolute/LIBNOVA_Research_Receiving_001.zip \
  --out /absolute/libnova-received
~~~

The snapshot includes the original bag, mapping, review, source ZIP where supplied, complete operation journals, provider observations, native IDs, job reports and receiving proof. It also includes the producer, client, requirements and original preservation/OAI application dependencies. The complete Workbench export additionally preserves its original source workspace and operator history.

Receiving hashes and extracts the same held archive descriptor. It validates the exact ZIP inventory and every member hash, then publishes the complete receiving directory atomically. A stopped extraction can continue its own bound staging files. An empty stage or interrupted binding write is recovered without accepting unrelated bytes.

Reopening the same archive at the same received destination preserves later legitimate progress and observations. It revalidates the original immutable application and operation members, including the operation/configuration identity. Deleting an original operation record does not turn into a successful reuse. Only the saved atomic state is allowed to advance under that original history.

After receiving, continue with the received application and its received workspace. Supply the same authorized environment references if a new remote observation is needed. Local verification and show require no tenant credentials. Do not discard the original receiving ZIP until the chosen durable destination has returned its actual file receipt.

## Acceptance and handoff

For one agreed deployment, retain the entered source/mapping agreement, original review revision, package ID, operation ID, container/storage/schema/Function IDs, native File index, original job ID, all job assets, source/content/metadata proofs and complete exported workspace.

Acceptance should demonstrate that every included record and original member is accounted for, original unmapped metadata remains present, the receiving reports describe the actual observation and the portable workspace reopens without another upload or job. A local fixture establishes the application's behavior against its pinned protocol; the receiving institution's acceptance establishes its deployed configuration.

This module implements the protocol independently. It does not redistribute the entire upstream LIBNOVA SDK as if all files shared one license. See LIBNOVA_PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md for the exact upstream source revisions, API shapes and limitations used in the implementation.

# Preservica provider contract

This document describes the exact package and API contract implemented by
`preservica.py` and `preservica_client.py`. It separates source/package verification,
an upload receipt, an observed ingest process, and verified repository content.
An existing Preservica deployment, its supported API version, its active ingest
configuration, and the intended archival parent remain explicit receiving inputs.

The initial receiving dataset is the original 169-record CC0 bibliographic
metadata example. Every included work becomes one original JSON content file with
a reviewed Dublin Core sidecar. This profile does not fetch or license paper full
text, media, or publisher attachments.

## Authority and version scope

The package format comes from Preservica's official
[Open Preservation Exchange documentation](https://developers.preservica.com/documentation/open-preservation-exchange-opex).
Preservica describes OPEX as its principal import/export format and documents
folder sidecars, content sidecars, immediate manifests, SourceID, security tags,
Dublin Core fragments, and supported fixity algorithms. Its
[OPEX/PAX ingest article](https://developers.preservica.com/blog/using-opex-and-pax-for-ingesting-content)
documents ordinary zipped OPEX ingest from version 6.2. The selected profile is
`preservica-opex-1.0-standard-ingest`; it uses the namespace
`http://www.openpreservationexchange.org/opex/v1.0`.

The upload interface comes from the official
[S3-compatible upload API](https://developers.preservica.com/api-reference/3-upload-content-s3-compatible).
The API explicitly supports the `Preservica-Access-Token` header, ordinary PUT,
HEAD, multipart initialization, part PUT, and multipart completion. The client
does not assume the full Amazon S3 API is available. In particular, it does not
invent list-parts, list-multipart-uploads, or object-download recovery endpoints.

The official [progress-token](https://developers.preservica.com/api-reference/4-progress-token-api)
and [process-monitoring](https://developers.preservica.com/api-reference/5-process-monitoring-api)
pages link to deployment Swagger documentation. Public demo documentation returned
403 during source intake; no successful current tenant Swagger capture is
represented here. The implemented entity and monitor response parsing is also
bound to the inspected primary implementation:
[carj/pyPreservica at 5a53e7e219ac16d28a5c77640518a596c0e8c088](https://github.com/carj/pyPreservica/tree/5a53e7e219ac16d28a5c77640518a596c0e8c088).

| `pyPreservica/monitorAPI.py` | `8a14d098d0c24730bdd6d457b3a50e2943623195` |

These sources were inspected on 12 October 2026. They are an explicit,
version-scoped implementation reference. They are not a claim that a particular
customer tenant has enabled the API, selected the required workflow, or accepted
this transfer. The standard-library client does not install or execute
pyPreservica.

Before upload, the client reads
`GET /api/entity/versiondetails/version` and compares the returned
`CurrentVersion` major/minor to the saved configuration. Entity/XIP namespaces
are derived from that explicit version, following the inspected implementation:
`http://preservica.com/EntityAPI/v<major.minor>` and
`http://preservica.com/XIP/v<major.minor>`. A different version stops the
operation for review. The template's 9.3 is an editable example, not a discovered
tenant property.

## Native package

The final upload is `transfer.zip`. It contains one top-level collection
directory, a `records` directory, and exactly one JSON content file plus OPEX
sidecar per included research record.

| Native member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `research-opex-<id>/research-opex-<id>.opex` | Package title, description, SourceID, selected/inherited security and package Dublin Core; manifest names the immediate `records` folder. |
| `research-opex-<id>/records/records.opex` | Records-folder SourceID and immediate file manifest. Each content and metadata file has its actual byte size and type. |
| `research-opex-<id>/records/W<id>.json` | Exact original canonical work JSON retained by the source export. |
| `research-opex-<id>/records/W<id>.json.opex` | SourceID, reviewed title/description/DC, original research identifier, original filename and SHA-256 fixity. |

A sidecar is not listed as its own folder's child. Folder manifests list immediate
children, not recursive paths. File sizes and SHA-256 values are computed from
the actual bytes written to the ZIP. Verification regenerates expected sidecars
from the retained original source and saved review, then streams every native
ZIP member to compare its name, size, CRC and SHA-256.

The record SourceID includes the immutable package identity and original work ID:
`<namespace>:edition:<package-id>:record:W<id>`. Package and records-folder
SourceIDs use distinct names. A different source edition, saved review or package
setting produces a different package identity. The original full OpenAlex
identifier remains in the reviewed metadata and identifiers; it is not replaced
by the ingest identifier.

Preservica's documented duplicate settings can use SourceID globally or locally.
This tool neither changes those settings nor guesses them. Reuse the saved
original upload operation when continuing it. Creating another operation or
altering the archival parent is an explicit operator decision subject to the
deployment's deduplication policy.

A null security tag omits the security descriptor and permits the documented
inheritance behavior. A non-null value must name an existing security tag; the
client checks the returned explicit tag during readback. Unknown security tags
are not silently created.

`original.zip` is the maintained preservation foundation's complete reviewed
source/evidence transfer, retained beside the native ZIP. It is not substituted
for the OPEX upload. `source-workspace/` keeps the editable source and complete
committed review ancestry. Complete alternate immutable review candidates from
an interrupted save are retained and labeled unpublished; `current.json` and
its exact prior-review links determine the committed chain.

## Configuration and credentials

`validate_settings` and `validate_configuration` are public offline
validators. They return normalized dictionaries and reject unknown fields. The
browser must invoke them before saving a package or upload plan.

| Client field | Validation and effect |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | `stellar-forge.preservica-configuration.v1`. |
| `origin` | One HTTPS origin with no path, credentials, query or fragment. Plain HTTP is accepted only for an explicitly selected literal loopback/local receiving service. |
| `tenant` | Existing tenant identifier. The upload bucket is derived as lower-case tenant plus `.package.upload`. |
| `targetVersion` | Entered major/minor, 6.2 or later; checked against the provider's version response. |
| `accessTokenEnv` | Environment variable name, never the access-token value. |
| `parentRef` | Explicit existing structural-object UUID, or null for the selected tenant root. |
| `uploadMode` | `auto`, `single`, or `multipart`. Auto uses a single PUT when the ZIP fits one configured part. |
| `partBytes` | 5 MiB–128 MiB; default 8 MiB. The final part may be smaller. |
| `requestTimeoutSeconds` | 1–300 seconds; default 60. |
| `maxResponseBytes` | 64 KiB–64 MiB; default 8 MiB for metadata/error responses. Original content downloads use their exact expected size. |
| `readbackBatchSize` | 1–250 records; default 25. All ready records are processed in the same run; the batch size controls saved progress. |

The current official [access-token documentation](https://developers.preservica.com/api-reference/6-access-token-api)
describes short-lived tokens and separate login/refresh endpoints. This client
uses an existing authorized token supplied by the receiving environment. A 401
returns `AUTH_REQUIRED`; after the environment is refreshed, the same operation
can continue. It does not retain passwords, token values, cookies or login
requests and does not create an account.

The object key is deterministic from the saved operation ID and transfer SHA-256.
It is not a free-form field. The parent is passed using the documented
`x-amz-meta-structuralobjectreference` header.

## HTTP and upload receipt semantics

The operation directory retains a request before dispatch and a response before
parsing it. Request records contain the exact method, safe selected URL, URL
digest, source-body digest/range and safe headers. Access-token values are
excluded. Responses retain status, safe headers, byte count, source digest,
completeness and any transport failure. Where a response contains a bearer token
or signed foreign URL, its retained text is redacted and its original byte
identity remains explicit. Original content is streamed and hashed; the upload
archive already retains the original bytes.

A final response name appears after its bytes have been written and synced.
Complete HTTP responses require a finished Content-Length/chunked body, not
merely HTTP 200. Conflicting ETag, progress-token, Content-Length, Location or
Retry-After values are rejected. A 200 response containing an S3 Error document
does not confirm a multipart completion.

| Action | Preserved identity | Receiving rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial HEAD | Original bucket/key | Records whether that unique key was absent before a first upload. HEAD 404 after an uncertain dispatch does not authorize a new upload. |
| Single PUT | Original ZIP digest and immutable key | Sent once unless the recorded response definitively rejected it before acceptance. A lost response remains uncertain. |
| Multipart initialization | Original key, request SHA and returned upload ID | A lost response requires the original response evidence. No undocumented upload listing is invented. |
| Part PUT | Upload ID, part number, exact byte range and SHA | May repeat the same part with the same bytes after a lost part response. Other parts keep their original receipts. |
| Completion POST | Same upload ID and ordered saved part ETags | A lost completion is not blindly repeated. Retained original response/progress or full source readback is reconciled. |
| HEAD progress observation | Same original key | A returned progress header/ETag may locate progress. Object presence is not a content/fixity acceptance result. |

ETags are opaque provider values. They are not assumed to be MD5 checksums.
The official API documents a progress-token response header and a
`-progressToken-<token>` suffix in completion ETags. If both occur they must
agree. The client preserves every earlier request and response when a later
observation resolves an uncertainty.

No automatic abort, delete, replacement upload or new operation is used to
clear an uncertain state. Incomplete multipart uploads are subject to the
provider's lifecycle; if the original upload has expired, its history remains
visible and a new, explicitly chosen operation needs a separately reviewed plan.

## Progress and process observation

The progress reader uses
`GET /api/entity/progress/{token}` and the
`{http://status.preservica.com}Status` element. The inspected implementation
enumerates ACTIVE, PENDING, COMPLETED, SUSPENDING, SUSPENDED, UNKNOWN, ABORTED,
FAILED, FINISHED_MIXED_OUTCOME and CANCELLED.

The process monitor is separate. The official
[Preservica 6.3 API summary](https://developers.preservica.com/blog/api-summary-in-preservica-6-3)
explicitly distinguished progress tokens and process identifiers in that release.
The inspected current SDK adds no progress-to-process mapping. Accordingly this
client does not infer one from a title, timestamp, queue order or successful
monitor status.

A supplied original process selection is observed through
`GET /api/processmonitor/monitors` and
`GET /api/processmonitor/messages?monitor=<id>&start=0&max=100`.
Every message must return the chosen `mappedMonitorId`. Pagination stays on
the same authenticated origin and endpoint and preserves the selected monitor.
The SDK's monitor documentation warns that mapped IDs can change between
releases. Saved process IDs are therefore observed receipts, not permanent
repository entity links. Absence from an unpaged monitor response is not claimed
as exhaustive absence.

A FAILED or mixed progress outcome remains `INGEST_FAILED` even if some files
are visible. Those files retain their individual readback receipts. A selected
process observation does not overwrite a stable SourceID/entity association.

## Full repository readback

The source-ID query is
`GET /api/entity/entities/by-identifier?type=SourceID&value=<exact-value>`.
It must return one entity of the expected type. The parser retains complete
paging when provided; it refuses changed query selection, inconsistent totals,
loops or ambiguous results.

The package and records folders are read as structural objects. Each work is
read as an information object. Original identifiers, title, parent and explicit
security are checked using the returned entity and identifier responses. Reviewed
DC is read through the exact metadata-fragment link in that entity and compared
by field/value multiplicity. An unrelated fragment is not accepted as a match.

The content route follows returned preservation representations, content-object
references, original generations and bitstreams. It checks the content-object
parent, exactly one original source filename, size and SHA-256 fixity. It then
streams the returned original content and verifies its actual byte count and
SHA-256 against the preserved JSON. Same-origin API links retain authentication;
a provider-issued cross-origin HTTPS content redirect receives no bearer token.
All final API/source links and source digests are retained.

`VERIFIED` requires both source folders and every included work to have
verified parent/SourceID/DC/content/fixity observations. A 200 upload, COMPLETED
token or Succeeded process does not by itself meet that condition. Excluded
records remain in the source catalog and review history but are not uploaded or
silently counted as received.

The client continues the entire ready cohort, saving progress after each batch.
A subsequent observation reuses already verified immutable receiving evidence
and works on the unresolved records. It does not present these historical
receipts as continuous monitoring of later repository edits.

## Recovery evidence

`reconciliation_template(kind)` exposes three exact JSON forms:

- `original-response`: original operation, action, request SHA, HTTP status,
  safe headers, base64 original response body, original observation time and
  source description. Init/complete XML must still name the original key and
  bucket. A confirmed response cannot be replaced with a different one.
- `progress-observation`: original single/complete request SHA, exact
  bucket/key and a token from the retained original response. This is labeled an
  explicit original-response association; source readback remains mandatory.
- `process-observation`: explicit original monitor ID and source
  description. Its scope remains an operator-selected process observation.

The client validates these inputs and retains their source descriptions and
hashes. Operator-supplied evidence is not represented as cryptographically
recovered signed provider material. Evidence cannot alter the original request,
configuration, source package, parent, upload key or part bytes.

## Concurrency and portable receiving

Producer/source changes use the foundation's `p.project_lock` / workspace.lock.
A running client holds one `remote/<operation>/operation.lock`. It takes the
ordinary package workspace lock only while publishing journal files or an atomic
current-state pointer. Network requests run outside that lock.

This permits the workbench to show local progress immediately and export a
consistent saved prefix. An export made during a request may correctly retain a
DISPATCHED/uncertain action; receiving that export does not turn it into an
unattempted action. Runtime lock files are excluded. Stop the original writer
before moving execution to another host; a filesystem lock is not a lock across
two independent copies.

Complete exports contain frozen source/review history, the original evidence
transfer, OPEX ZIP, all upload/readback journals, and the complete receiving
application. Export/receive verify every member's size, CRC and SHA. Existing
outputs are reconciled or refused if they represent a different revision; they
are not overwritten to hide later work.

The implementation's native ZIP limit is 4 GiB and portable snapshot limit is
8 GiB. The underlying research foundation still reads some original members in
memory. These are format/implementation bounds, not a measured throughput claim
or a 20 GB engagement promise. The initial commercial scope is limited to 1,000
bibliographic metadata records and 1 GiB source/export material, subject to the
agreed sample. Actual evidence for this source profile begins with the original
169-record example.

## What remains deployment-specific

The selected customer must provide an existing tenant, supported version,
authorized token reference, archival parent, security policy and an active
standard ingest configuration compatible with zipped OPEX. Actual tenant upload,
workflow acceptance and final repository readback must be recorded against that
deployment. The local native receiving journey demonstrates the complete
implemented package/HTTP/recovery/portable contract; it is labeled separately
from customer tenant acceptance.

# Preservica research package and receiving guide

This workflow carries a saved bibliographic review into a native OPEX ingest
package, then keeps the original upload and repository verification together.
Use the common browser workbench for source review and saved operations, or the
Python commands below. Both routes call the same producer and client.

The original example contains 169 CC0 OpenAlex metadata records. Each included
record becomes one JSON content asset with reviewed Dublin Core. Paper full text
and publisher attachments are outside this source profile. The existing source
export, selected decisions, corrections, exclusions and complete review ancestry
remain in the final handoff.

Read [PRESERVICA_PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md](PRESERVICA_PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md) for exact
endpoint, response, source and version boundaries, and [WORKBENCH.md](WORKBENCH.md)
for the shared browser flow. The separate engagement proposal is not an API or
deployment-readiness guarantee.

## Before receiving

Use Python 3.11 or later on Linux with the complete application directory. The
producer and client use the standard library and the existing preservation
foundation. No vendor SDK installation, account creation or hosted CI is needed.

For an actual repository operation, select one existing tenant and its supported
major/minor API version. Obtain the original archival-parent UUID or deliberately
select the tenant root; confirm its standard zipped-OPEX ingest configuration and
security policy. Supply an authorized current access token through an
environment variable on the receiving host. Put only that variable's name in the
configuration and browser.

The documented zipped OPEX profile requires Preservica 6.2 or later. The actual
tenant version is checked before upload. A template containing an example origin
or tenant cannot be saved as a real operation.

## 1. Open the original source and save the review

Run commands from the directory containing `preservation.py`,
`preservica.py` and `preservica_client.py`.

```bash
python3 preservation.py init \
  --source /path/to/OpenAlex_CIIM_Source_Example_20261012.zip \
  --prefix source-export \
  --workspace /path/to/source-workspace

python3 preservation.py show --workspace /path/to/source-workspace

python3 preservation.py review-template \
  --workspace /path/to/source-workspace > /path/to/review.json
```

Edit the review document using the existing schema. Record a reason when
correcting metadata or excluding a work. The source record and original
metadata remain preserved. Then save against the revision you actually read:

```bash
python3 preservation.py review-save \
  --workspace /path/to/source-workspace \
  --input /path/to/review.json \
  --expected-revision 0
```

The command returns the new revision. A stale revision refuses the save; reload
the current review and retain the later user's changes. The browser uses the
same revision check.

A complete immutable review file can survive a crash before the current pointer
is updated. The Preservica producer follows the selected pointer and exact
previous-review hashes to freeze the committed chain. Other complete candidates
remain explicitly unpublished; their presence does not erase or block the
selected review.

## 2. Prepare a native package at that exact revision

```bash
python3 preservica.py settings-template > /path/to/preservica-settings.json
```

The normalized settings object is:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.preservica-package-settings.v1",
  "title": "Reviewed research metadata",
  "description": "Original bibliographic metadata with source provenance and explicit review decisions.",
  "securityTag": null,
  "sourceIdNamespace": "urn:commons:research",
  "sourceIdPolicy": "edition-record",
  "opexNamespace": "http://www.openpreservationexchange.org/opex/v1.0",
  "targetPreservicaVersion": null
}
```

Use an existing security tag, or leave it null to preserve documented inheritance.
An optional target version binds the package to that selected major/minor; a
null version means the tenant has not yet been selected. Package verification
does not imply that a null-version package has been accepted by any deployment.

Prepare from the actual saved revision, for example revision 1:

```bash
python3 preservica.py prepare \
  --workspace /path/to/source-workspace \
  --out /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --expected-revision 1 \
  --settings /path/to/preservica-settings.json

python3 preservica.py verify \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1
```

The prepared directory includes:

| File or directory | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `transfer.zip` | Native zipped OPEX payload for the selected upload. |
| `original.zip` | Complete original reviewed-source transfer and provenance. |
| `source-workspace/` | Reopenable source, current review, committed history and retained unpublished candidates. |
| `catalog.json` / `catalog.csv` | All original records, review decisions, SourceIDs and exact native paths/byte identities. |
| `review.html` | Standalone readable source/package review. |
| `settings.json` | Normalized selected package settings. |
| `source-members.json` | Original evidence-member identities. |
| `handoff.json` / `MANIFEST.json` | Source/review/native-format identity and complete immutable prepared inventory. |
| `remote/` | Created later for saved upload, progress and readback operations. |

Verification regenerates the expected OPEX metadata from the retained source
and selected review, then checks every native member and its bytes. This is
package verification; the initial repository state is `NOT_SUBMITTED`.

Preparing again into the same destination with exactly the same source,
revision and settings reopens the original package. A changed selection requires
a new destination. To compare two prepared editions:

```bash
python3 preservica.py compare \
  --before /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --after /path/to/preservica-package-r2
```

## 3. Save an explicit repository operation

Generate and edit the client configuration:

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py configuration-template \
  > /path/to/preservica-configuration.json
```

The complete field set is:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.preservica-configuration.v1",
  "origin": "https://YOUR-TENANT.preservica.com",
  "tenant": "YOUR_TENANT",
  "targetVersion": "9.3",
  "accessTokenEnv": "PRESERVICA_ACCESS_TOKEN",
  "parentRef": null,
  "uploadMode": "auto",
  "partBytes": 8388608,
  "requestTimeoutSeconds": 60,
  "maxResponseBytes": 8388608,
  "readbackBatchSize": 25
}
```

Replace the example tenant, origin and version with the actual agreed deployment.
Choose the real parent. The template is deliberately rejected until the
placeholders are replaced. Unknown configuration fields and literal credentials
are rejected. The access token's value belongs only in the authorized runtime
environment.

Save one stable original operation ID:

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py plan \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --configuration /path/to/preservica-configuration.json \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012

python3 preservica_client.py show \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012
```

Planning is offline. It binds the source, review, native archive, target, parent,
token-environment reference, upload mode and original object key. It does not
upload or sign in. Reusing the operation ID with different settings refuses the
change. Keep this same ID for normal run, refresh and reconciliation.

## 4. Run the original upload and complete receiving

Once the selected environment contains the authorized current token:

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py run \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012
```

The client verifies the package, reads the selected tenant version and parent,
and checks the original unique upload key. It retains each original request
before dispatch and its response before interpreting the provider result.

A small ZIP uses one PUT in auto mode. Multipart mode retains its original
upload ID and each part's exact range, SHA and ETag. A part may resend the same
bytes to the same part number after transport loss. Initialization and completion
remain their original operations; a lost response does not cause a replacement
upload or another completion.

After upload, the same invocation observes progress and processes all repository
records that are ready. It saves progress every configured batch. A batch size
of 25 does not require seven manual submissions for the 169-record example.

For each included work, receiving verifies:

1. The exact SourceID returns one information object.
2. The object has the selected records-folder parent, expected title, retained
   original identifier and any explicitly selected security tag.
3. The returned metadata fragment contains the reviewed DC values with the same
   field/value multiplicity.
4. The original preservation content has the expected filename, byte size and
   SHA-256 fixity.
5. A full streamed content read produces the original source bytes' SHA-256.

The package and records folders are also verified against their original
SourceIDs and selected parent. A completed upload or successful process status
does not replace these checks.

The result is JSON containing `state`, `transfer`, `ingest`,
`readback`, `actions`, `retryAt`, safe target observations and next actions.
The workbench renders the same result. Local status reads remain available
while the background client holds its separate operation lock.

| Observed state | Meaning and normal next action |
| --- | --- |
| `PLANNED` | Saved offline selection; use run after the agreed access is ready. |
| `UPLOADING` | Original upload action is active or retained before dispatch completion. |
| `UPLOAD_UNCERTAIN` | Original response/dispatch needs reconciliation; do not create a replacement operation. |
| `INGESTING` | Upload/progress is pending or source entities are not yet available. |
| `VERIFYING` | Some original records are received; unresolved source or content checks remain. |
| `COOLDOWN` | Provider Retry-After is saved. Continue after that time using the same operation. |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | Supply a fresh authorized token in the same named environment variable. |
| `INTERRUPTED` | Cancellation was observed between/within requests; inspect the retained original action and continue. |
| `NEEDS_REVIEW` | Version, response or source contract needs a concrete operator/source decision. |
| `INGEST_FAILED` | Original progress reports failure or mixed outcome. Existing per-file evidence remains. |
| `VERIFIED` | Both source folders and every included record have complete retained receiving evidence. |

## 5. Observe or reconcile without repeating an unknown write

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py refresh \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012
```

Refresh performs provider reads and local evidence updates. It does not issue
an upload PUT or multipart initialization/completion POST. It resumes unresolved
record verification and reuses previously verified immutable receiving receipts.
Those receipts describe when the content was observed; they do not claim
continuous monitoring of later repository changes.

A lost initialization/completion response can be recovered from the actual
original response retained by the operator or another authorized system:

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py reconciliation-template --kind original-response \
  > /path/to/original-response.json
```

Fill the template with the exact original operation ID, action and request SHA
shown in `show.actions`; the original HTTP status and safe headers; base64 of
the complete original response XML; its observation time; and a description of
its retained source. Do not include authentication headers or cookies. Do not
construct a successful response from guessed IDs.

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py reconcile \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012 \
  --evidence /path/to/original-response.json
```

The XML still must name the original bucket/key and upload identity. Reconcile
retains the earlier uncertainty and new source receipt. It cannot change the
original package, parent, request, byte ranges or configuration.

Two additional templates are available:

```bash
python3 preservica_client.py reconciliation-template --kind progress-observation
python3 preservica_client.py reconciliation-template --kind process-observation
```

A progress observation binds a token from the original upload response to the
same original request and key. A process observation explicitly selects a
returned monitor ID and records its source. The client does not equate progress
tokens with process IDs or infer a process from matching titles/times. Monitor
IDs remain observed receipts; they may change across product releases.

A 404 for an old progress token or upload key does not prove that a prior upload
never happened. A missing or contradictory response stays visible while source
readback and the original provider evidence are reconciled.

## 6. Export the complete operation and reopen it

Stop the original writer before handing execution to another host. The export
can capture a consistent saved prefix during an active request, but two copied
workspaces do not share a filesystem lock.

Use a new filename for a later journal/review snapshot:

```bash
python3 preservica.py export \
  --workspace /path/to/preservica-package-r1 \
  --out /path/to/Research_Preservica_Receiving_20261012.zip

python3 preservica.py receive \
  --source /path/to/Research_Preservica_Receiving_20261012.zip \
  --out /path/to/received-research
```

The complete export contains the prepared package and original evidence, editable
source/review history, upload/progress/readback journals, all reports and the
complete receiving application. Every member is checked by name, length, CRC and
SHA-256. Runtime locks and private unfinished writes are omitted. Existing
exports are reused only if their exact original contents match; later state
needs a new filename.

The received package is under `received-research/workspace/`, with the
application under `received-research/application/research/preservation/`.
Supply the same authorized token environment reference on the receiving host,
then use its included client:

```bash
python3 /path/to/received-research/application/research/preservation/preservica_client.py show \
  --workspace /path/to/received-research/workspace \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012

python3 /path/to/received-research/application/research/preservation/preservica_client.py refresh \
  --workspace /path/to/received-research/workspace \
  --operation-id research-ingest-20261012
```

A retained unknown dispatch remains unknown in the received workspace. Refresh
and original-response evidence provide the same recovery paths. Restoring a
package does not silently submit it to a different tenant.

## Callable interface for integrations

```python
import preservica
import preservica_client

settings = preservica.validate_settings(selected_settings)
prepared = preservica.prepare(
    source_workspace, package_workspace, expected_revision,
    settings=settings,
)
preservica.verify_workspace(package_workspace)

configuration = preservica_client.validate_configuration(selected_configuration)
planned = preservica_client.plan(package_workspace, configuration, operation_id)
status = preservica_client.show(package_workspace, operation_id)

result = preservica_client.run(
    package_workspace, operation_id, cancelled=cancelled_callback,
)
observed = preservica_client.refresh(
    package_workspace, operation_id, cancelled=cancelled_callback,
)
reconciled = preservica_client.reconcile(
    package_workspace, operation_id, original_evidence,
    cancelled=cancelled_callback,
)
exported = preservica.export(package_workspace, output_zip)
received = preservica.receive(output_zip, receiving_directory)
```

Validators return normalized dictionaries. The source foundation's
`p.project_lock` protects review/package changes. Client run/reconcile has a
separate operation lock and takes the ordinary package lock only while
publishing journals/state. The browser's nonblocking status path is the same
`preservica_client.show` function.

## Limits and acceptance record

The native ZIP bound is 4 GiB and the portable snapshot bound is 8 GiB; these are
implementation limits, not throughput measurements. Some original-source
foundation paths still load members into memory. The proposed initial engagement
therefore uses a narrower envelope: up to 1,000 bibliographic metadata records
and 1 GiB source/export material, subject to the supplied sample and selected
deployment.

The full original 169-record native receiving operation records package
verification, actual local HTTP upload/recovery, source/entity/DC/file/fixity
checks and portable reopen. Its receipt must say explicitly whether the endpoint
was the local contract service or an agreed Preservica tenant. No local outcome
should be presented as a customer tenant ingest.

For an actual delivery retain the final source manifest, package and journal
snapshot, original operation ID, actual endpoint/version, target parent, complete
record/file counts, unresolved exceptions, all observed source/fixity receipts,
and the original provider/process IDs with their proper scopes. Preserve the
unchanged historical source alongside any later review or receiving edition.
